messages:
kevin: Observed a weird edge in the onboarding sampleapp: when a prefetch request hits a 429 with Retry-After, our backoff can push the retry past the server's cursor TTL and the retried request returns a stale-cursor error. That then triggers a fallback that re-requests from an earlier cursor and we get duplicates/skips. Anyone seen this?

izumi: interesting. which SDK & sampleapp? JS? Go?

kevin: JS sampleapp on staging. config: prefetch=5, concurrency=10, backoff=max 60s. server cursor TTL seems to be ~30s based on debug headers. Logs: 

```
DBG send prefetch cursor=cA req_id=R1
DBG response 429 Retry-After=25s req_id=R1
DBG backoff scheduled 25s req_id=R1
DBG other prefetches advance cursor -> latest=cD
DBG retry req_id=R1 after 25s -> 400 cursor_expired
DBG fallback start from safe-cursor=cB -> duplicates
```

parker: OK that is new. So Retry-After delays > cursor TTL. Server magic: cursors are ephemeral unless pinned. If client retries blindly it can hit cursor_expired. We should either: clamp client backoff to a fraction of cursor TTL, or include a cursor_epoch/ttl stamp in the request and skip retry when epoch != current.

rachel: SDK parity note: python sdk recently added a `paginator.pinCursor()` that renews cursor server-side; not enabled in JS. Could help but is heavier for clients. Another option: on 429 we prefer to re-issue a fresh fetch from latest cursor rather than replaying the original request payload. That avoids stale cursor replays but may lose the exact page boundary guarantees.

kevin: idea: add lightweight metadata to each request header: X-Cursor-Epoch and X-Prefetch-Stamp (iso ts). Server can return X-Cursor-TTL in 429 and we can auto-clamp backoff to min(retryAfter, ttl*0.6). Also if epoch != current, the retry handler drops the replay and fetches latest cursor instead.

izumi: we should be cautious: forcing a fetch-from-latest silently changes app semantics. Better to expose a `retryStrategy` hook to the SDK consumer with options: replay, refresh-and-fetch-latest, or drop. Default should be safe for typical paging: refresh-and-fetch-latest for prefetch flows.

parker: agree. Also emit telemetry when a replay is dropped or when backoff is clamped: metric `paginator.retry_policy.action` with tags {action:clamped|dropped|replayed, sdk:js, tenant:<tenant>}. That will help customers debug.

rachel: for parity: implement `retryStrategy` in JS and Go next sprint, and a feature flag `paginator_cursor_epoch` we can flip for early testing. Python and C# teams can follow same API surface.

kevin: for immediate workaround in sampleapp I lowered backoff max to 10s and set prefetch=2; that eliminated duplicates in local stress test. I'll open a PR with a short doc blurb explaining cursor TTL interactions.

infra-bot: Created issue #5110: "paginator: retries + Retry-After can exceed cursor TTL -> duplicate pages"

izumi: can you add a tiny test harness that mocks 429 Retry-After and enforces cursor TTL expiration to catch this in CI?

kevin: yes will add e2e that injects 429 with Retry-After and asserts no duplicates under new retryStrategy.

parker: one more: server could include a `retry_guidance` header that suggests safe backoff window per-tenant. We can respect that if present. Add to proposal doc.

kevin: will include header suggestions + samplecode for `retryStrategy` in the PR. pinging @rachel for API parity review when ready.

rachel: will review. Thanks for catching this, good to make retry behavior paginated-aware. :slightly_smiling_face:
